# Speaking Coach

> Speaking Coach: practice interviews, speeches and small talk out loud, with an AI partner, in 20 languages.

Speaking Coach is an iPhone and Android app by Sodhera Intelligence (https://apps.apple.com/app/id6767124039, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sodhera.speakingcoach), with a free voice review in ChatGPT. These pages answer common questions about interviews, speeches, presentations and conversations. Each page has a Markdown copy at index.md.

## Free speaking tools

- [Conversation practice drill: keep it going out loud](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/conversation-drill/index.md): Practice three conversation skills out loud: asking follow-up questions, sharing something of your own and ending politely. 12 prompts, free, in your browser.
- [Filler word counter: count your ums and uhs (free)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/filler-word-counter/index.md): Speak or paste a transcript and count your filler words: um, uh, like, you know and more. Free, runs in your browser, no sign-up.
- [Free speech review: check your pace and filler words](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/free-speech-review/index.md): Speak a speech, toast or talk and see your words per minute, filler words, long pauses and a transcript. Free, runs in your browser, no sign-up.
- [Practice interview answers out loud: free answer check](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/interview-answer-review/index.md): Answer 12 classic interview questions out loud and see your pace, filler words, long pauses and transcript. Free, in your browser, no sign-up.
- [Interview questions by role: find questions for your job](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/interview-questions-by-role/index.md): Type your job title and see the interview questions you're likely to get for that role, then open the full guide with how to answer each one.
- [Speaking pace checker: measure your words per minute, free](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/pace-checker/index.md): Find your speaking rate in words per minute by talking or by entering a word count and a time. See typical ranges and how to slow down or speed up.
- [Small talk practice drill: answer openers out loud](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/small-talk-drill/index.md): Practice small talk by replying out loud to 15 everyday openers a stranger might say. See your reply length, pace, fillers and transcript. Free.
- [Speech length calculator: words to minutes (and back)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/tools/speech-length-calculator/index.md): Turn a word count into speaking time, or minutes into words, at slow, average and fast pace. With a quick table for 1 to 20 minute speeches.

## Common interview questions and how to answer them

- [Are you interviewing with other companies? How to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/are-you-interviewing-with-other-companies/index.md): How to answer 'Are you interviewing with other companies?' honestly without weakening your position or naming companies, with lines for every stage of your search.
- [Aren't you overqualified for this job? How to answer the concern](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/are-you-overqualified-for-this-job/index.md): How to answer 'Aren't you overqualified?': name the real worry (pay, boredom or leaving soon), answer it with your actual reason, and show you'll stay.
- [Are you planning higher studies or an MBA? How to answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/are-you-planning-higher-studies/index.md): How to answer 'Are you planning higher studies?' in a campus HR round: what the interviewer fears, honest answers for each situation, and lines to avoid.
- [Are you willing to relocate? How to answer if you're unsure](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/are-you-willing-to-relocate/index.md): How to answer 'Are you willing to relocate?' with a yes, a no or 'it depends', and how to ask about relocation support without putting the offer at risk.
- [Are you willing to work overtime or weekends? How to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/are-you-willing-to-work-overtime/index.md): How to answer 'Are you willing to work overtime or weekends?' honestly: say what you can do, name real limits, and ask how often extra hours actually happen.
- [Describe yourself in three words: interview answers with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/describe-yourself-in-three-words/index.md): Pick three words that fit the job, back each with one sentence, and avoid overused ones. Word lists by role type and example answers for four jobs.
- [Do you have any questions for us? What to ask at the end](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/do-you-have-any-questions-for-us/index.md): What to ask at the end of an interview, by stage: recruiter screen, hiring manager, team and final round. How many to bring, and which questions to avoid.
- [Do you prefer working alone or in a team? How to answer it well](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/do-you-prefer-working-alone-or-in-a-team/index.md): How to answer 'Do you prefer working alone or in a team?': show you do both well, match the role's real mix, and give an example of each.
- [Have you ever been fired? How to answer the question honestly](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/have-you-ever-been-fired/index.md): How to answer 'Have you ever been fired?' honestly: a short factual explanation, what you learned, and a bridge to why you're ready for this job.
- [How did you prepare for this interview? How to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-did-you-prepare-for-this-interview/index.md): How to answer 'How did you prepare for this interview?': name the research and practice you did, and share one thing you learned that excites you.
- [How do you handle criticism? How to answer with an example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-do-you-handle-criticism/index.md): How to answer 'How do you handle criticism?' without sounding defensive or fake: a short method, one real example of feedback you acted on, and lines to say.
- [How do you handle repetitive work? How to answer in an interview](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-do-you-handle-repetitive-work/index.md): How to answer 'How do you handle repetitive work?' for data entry, warehouse, admin and call center jobs: show accuracy, focus and a process you improved.
- [How do you handle stress and pressure? Interview answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-do-you-handle-stress-and-pressure/index.md): Describe the habits you use when pressure builds and prove them with one short story. What to stress for high-pressure roles, with four example answers.
- [How do you prioritize your work? Interview answer with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-do-you-prioritize-your-work/index.md): How to answer 'How do you prioritize your work?': explain your method in two sentences, then walk through a real busy week with competing demands and what you did.
- [How do you stay up to date in your field? Example answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-do-you-stay-up-to-date-in-your-field/index.md): How to answer 'How do you stay up to date in your field?': show a real learning habit, name your sources, and one thing you applied recently.
- [How do you work with people from different backgrounds? Answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-do-you-work-with-people-from-different-backgrounds/index.md): How to answer 'How do you work with people from different backgrounds?': show inclusive habits and one concrete example across cultures, ages or job functions.
- [How has your education prepared you for this job? Example answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-has-your-education-prepared-you-for-this-job/index.md): How to answer 'How has your education prepared you for this job?': map specific courses, projects and skills onto the job's needs, with examples.
- [How would you describe your work style? Interview answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-would-you-describe-your-work-style/index.md): How to describe your work style in an interview: say how you plan, communicate and finish work, with example answers for analysts, nurses, sales, creative roles and more.
- [How would you describe yourself? Interview answers with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-would-you-describe-yourself/index.md): A 30-second self-description in two or three traits, each with proof. How it differs from 'Tell me about yourself', plus examples for four roles.
- [How would you handle a task you don't know how to do?](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-would-you-handle-a-task-you-dont-know-how-to-do/index.md): How to answer 'How would you handle a task you don't know how to do?': research first, ask a clear question, check in early, so you sound capable, not helpless.
- [How would you handle an angry customer? Interview answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-would-you-handle-an-angry-customer/index.md): How to answer 'How would you handle an angry customer?' with a step-by-step de-escalation plan and the exact lines you'd say to the customer, plus a real example.
- [How would your coworkers describe you? How to answer honestly](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/how-would-your-coworkers-describe-you/index.md): How to answer 'How would your coworkers describe you?' using real feedback you've received: where to find it, how to quote it, and examples that don't sound inflated.
- [If we offered you the job, would you accept? How to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/if-we-offered-you-the-job-would-you-accept/index.md): How to answer 'If we offered you the job, would you accept?': show real enthusiasm while leaving room to review the full offer, with examples for each case.
- [If you were an animal, what would you be? Odd interview questions](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/if-you-were-an-animal-what-would-you-be/index.md): How to answer 'If you were an animal, what would you be?' and other curveball questions: why they're asked and a quick formula to link any one to work.
- [Is there anything else you would like to add? How to close well](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/is-there-anything-else-you-would-like-to-add/index.md): Use the last word in an interview well: a 30-second closing summary, how to repair a weak earlier answer, and example closes you can adapt.
- [Sell me this pen: how to answer the sales interview question](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/sell-me-this-pen/index.md): How to answer 'Sell me this pen' in a sales interview: ask questions first, pitch to the need you uncover, handle one objection and ask for the sale.
- [Tell me about a time you had to adapt to change: answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-adapted-to-change/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you had to adapt to change': pick a reorg, new tool or shifted goal and show how fast you got productive again.
- [Tell me about a time you dealt with ambiguity: how to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-dealt-with-ambiguity/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you dealt with ambiguity': show how you moved forward when goals were unclear, made sensible assumptions and got clarity.
- [Tell me about a time you disagreed with your boss: how to answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-disagreed-with-your-manager/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager': raise it privately with evidence, offer an option, then commit once they decide.
- [Tell me about a time you explained something complex simply](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-explained-something-complex/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you explained something complex' in a behavioral interview: who the audience was, how you adapted, and what changed.
- [Tell me about a challenge you faced: how to answer with STAR](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-faced-a-challenge/index.md): Pick a challenge of the right size and tell it with STAR: timing for each part, a measurable result, full example answers and follow-ups to prepare for.
- [Tell me about a time you faced an ethical dilemma: how to answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-faced-an-ethical-dilemma/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you faced an ethical dilemma': pick a dilemma that's real but safe to share, and show your reasoning and action.
- [Tell me about a time you failed: how to answer this question](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-failed/index.md): Own a real failure, explain what you changed afterwards, and avoid failures that are too big or too small to use. Example answers for four situations.
- [Tell me about a time you gave difficult feedback: answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-gave-difficult-feedback/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you gave difficult feedback': the words you used, how the person reacted, and what changed, for peers and direct reports.
- [Tell me about a conflict at work: how to answer, with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-had-a-conflict/index.md): Answer the conflict question with a peer story: raise it privately, find a shared goal, resolve it calmly and keep the relationship. STAR examples.
- [Tell me about a time you had to learn something quickly: answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-learned-something-quickly/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you had to learn something quickly': show your method for ramping up under a deadline, with examples for tools and subjects.
- [Tell me about a time you made a difficult decision: examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-made-a-difficult-decision/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you made a difficult decision': show the options, what you didn't know, why you chose, and that you owned the outcome.
- [Tell me about a time you made a mistake: answers with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-made-a-mistake/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you made a mistake': pick a real work error, explain how you caught and fixed it, and the check you added so it can't happen again.
- [Tell me about a time you met a tight deadline: answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-met-a-tight-deadline/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you met a tight deadline': show how you planned, what scope you cut, and who you told, with timings and numbers in STAR examples.
- [Tell me about a time you missed a deadline: how to answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-missed-a-deadline/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you missed a deadline': own the late delivery, show you warned people early, and name what you changed afterward.
- [Tell me about a time you persuaded someone: STAR answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-persuaded-someone/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you persuaded someone': influence without authority, using evidence and the other person's concerns, with examples.
- [Tell me about a time you showed leadership (with no title)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-showed-leadership/index.md): How to answer the leadership question when you've never managed anyone: where to find a story, how to structure it, and examples from projects, peers and school.
- [Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem at work](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-solved-a-problem/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem': show your reasoning steps, what you ruled out and why, not only the final fix.
- [Tell me about a time you took initiative: example answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-took-initiative/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you took initiative': a problem nobody asked you to fix, how you checked before acting, what you did and the result.
- [Tell me about a time you used data to make a decision: examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-used-data-to-make-a-decision/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you used data to make a decision': the question, the data you used, what it showed, what you decided and what happened.
- [Tell me about a time you went above and beyond: example answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-went-above-and-beyond/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you went above and beyond': show extra effort with a clear result, without implying you neglect your job or ignore boundaries.
- [Tell me about a time you were creative at work: example answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-were-creative/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me about a time you were creative': pick a new idea you actually tried, show why the old way fell short, and end on the measured difference.
- [Tell me about a time you worked in a team: STAR answer examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-a-time-you-worked-well-in-a-team/index.md): How to answer the teamwork interview question with STAR: show your specific role inside a group result, not just 'we did it', with example answers and a 'we vs I' check.
- [Tell me about your extracurricular activities: interview answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-your-extracurricular-activities/index.md): How to answer questions about extracurricular activities when you lack work experience: use clubs, sports and volunteering as proof of skills, with examples.
- [Tell me about your final year project: how to answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-your-final-year-project/index.md): How to explain your final year project in a campus interview: the problem, your part, the result and what you'd change, plus the technical follow-ups to expect.
- [Tell me about yourself: how to answer, with example answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-about-yourself/index.md): Answer 'Tell me about yourself' in 60–90 seconds with a present-past-future pitch. Example answers for graduates, career changers and experienced hires.
- [Tell me something that's not on your resume: how to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/tell-me-something-not-on-your-resume/index.md): How to answer 'Tell me something that's not on your resume': choosing a story the CV hides, a three-part structure, examples and topics to avoid.
- [Walk me through your resume: how to answer in under two minutes](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/walk-me-through-your-resume/index.md): A chronological walkthrough of your resume with each move explained, in under two minutes. Timing plan, transition lines, gaps and a full example.
- [What are you looking for in a new job? How to answer it well](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-are-you-looking-for-in-a-new-job/index.md): How to answer 'What are you looking for in a new job?': name three things you want that this job actually offers, so your answer doubles as a fit argument.
- [What are you passionate about? How to answer in an interview](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-are-you-passionate-about/index.md): How to answer 'What are you passionate about?' in an interview: pick something genuine, show it with a detail, and connect it to how you work without forcing it.
- [What are your current job responsibilities? How to answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-are-your-current-job-responsibilities/index.md): How to answer 'What are your current job responsibilities?' in about a minute: describe your duties by impact, not a task list, and link them to the new role.
- [What are your hobbies? How to answer in a job interview](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-are-your-hobbies/index.md): How to answer 'What are your hobbies?' in an interview: which hobbies to mention, how much detail to give, hobbies that backfire and example answers.
- [What are your salary expectations? How to answer with a range](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-are-your-salary-expectations/index.md): Research a salary range, decide when to name a number or defer, and use exact lines for early phone screens, later rounds and pushy follow-ups.
- [What are your short-term goals? Answers for freshers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-are-your-short-term-goals/index.md): How freshers can answer 'What are your short-term goals?': one or two concrete learning and contribution goals for the next 1-2 years, tied to this role.
- [What are your strengths? How to answer, with examples to use](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-are-your-strengths/index.md): Pick two or three strengths the job needs, back each with a short proof, and drop vague words like 'hard-working'. Example answers for four roles.
- [What did you learn from your internship? Example answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-did-you-learn-from-your-internship/index.md): How to answer 'What did you learn from your internship?': turn tasks into skills and results an employer cares about, with examples and a translation table.
- [What did you like least about your last job? How to answer safely](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-did-you-like-least-about-your-last-job/index.md): How to answer 'What did you like least about your last job?': name a real dislike about the work that this job doesn't have, without criticising people.
- [What did you think of your last boss? How to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-did-you-think-of-your-last-boss/index.md): How to answer 'What did you think of your last boss?', even about a bad one: one real strength, one thing you learned, and no criticism.
- [What do you expect from a manager? How to answer this question](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-do-you-expect-from-your-manager/index.md): How to answer 'What do you expect from your manager?': the support and feedback you work best with, without sounding high-maintenance.
- [What do you know about our company? How to answer and research](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-do-you-know-about-our-company/index.md): A 15-minute research routine and a four-part answer that turns facts into a link to the role. Example answers, weak vs strong uses, and common slips.
- [What would you do if a coworker wasn't doing their share of work?](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-if-a-coworker-is-not-doing-their-share/index.md): How to answer the question about a coworker not pulling their weight: check the facts, talk to them first, then escalate fairly. With lines you could say.
- [What would you do if two managers gave you conflicting tasks?](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-if-two-managers-give-conflicting-tasks/index.md): How to answer the question about conflicting tasks from two managers: raise it openly, give both the facts, and get one agreed order. With example lines.
- [What is the last book you read? How to answer in an interview](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-the-last-book-you-read/index.md): How to answer 'What is the last book you read?': pick a book you can discuss for two minutes, give one idea from it, and link that idea to how you work.
- [What is the lowest salary you would accept? How to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-the-lowest-salary-you-would-accept/index.md): How to answer 'What is the lowest salary you would accept?' without naming your floor: why your minimum hurts you and lines that keep negotiation open.
- [What is your biggest regret? How to answer without oversharing](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-biggest-regret/index.md): How to answer 'What is your biggest regret?' in an interview: pick a work regret, say what it taught you and what you do now, and keep personal topics out.
- [What is your current salary? How to answer or politely redirect](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-current-salary/index.md): How to answer 'What is your current salary?' or redirect to your expectations instead, with exact lines to say, and where to check if employers may ask at all.
- [What is your dream job? How to answer it in a job interview](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-dream-job/index.md): How to answer 'What is your dream job?' in an interview: describe the work and impact you want, not a title, and show how this role moves you toward it.
- [What is your favorite subject? Campus interview answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-favorite-subject/index.md): How to answer 'What is your favorite subject?' in a campus interview: choose one you can defend under technical follow-ups, how to prepare, and example answers.
- [What is your greatest achievement? How to answer, with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-greatest-achievement/index.md): Choose one achievement that fits the role, show what made it hard, and put a number on the result. Includes options and examples for graduates.
- [What is your greatest weakness? How to answer, with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-greatest-weakness/index.md): How to pick a real but safe weakness, show what you do about it, and avoid fake answers like 'I'm a perfectionist'. Examples for three career stages.
- [What is your ideal work environment? How to answer honestly](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-ideal-work-environment/index.md): How to answer 'What is your ideal work environment?' honestly: name two conditions you do your best work in, match them to this employer, and stay flexible.
- [What is your leadership style? How to answer, with examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-leadership-style/index.md): How to answer 'What is your leadership style?': name your style in plain words, prove it with a real team moment, and show you adjust it to the person.
- [What is your notice period? How to answer and negotiate it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-is-your-notice-period/index.md): How to answer 'What is your notice period?': state it exactly, mention early release or buyout options, and handle a 60 or 90 day notice calmly.
- [What makes you unique? How to answer this interview question](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-makes-you-unique/index.md): Find the combination of skills, experience or background other candidates lack, instead of a personality claim. A method, a worksheet and examples.
- [What motivates you? How to answer, with examples by job type](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-motivates-you/index.md): Name a motivator the role actually offers and prove it with a short story. Motivators by job type, ones that hurt you, and example answers for four jobs.
- [What would you do in your first 90 days? How to answer it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-would-you-do-in-your-first-90-days/index.md): How to answer 'What would you do in your first 90 days?': a learn-then-contribute plan for days 1-30, 31-60 and 61-90, with examples for different roles.
- [What would you improve about our company? How to answer tactfully](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interview-questions/what-would-you-improve-about-our-company/index.md): How to answer 'What would you improve about our company?': one researched, respectful idea about their product or service, framed as an opportunity.

Examples for four situations.

## Interview types and how to prepare for each

- [What happens at an assessment centre? How to prepare for the day](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/assessment-centre/index.md): Graduate assessment centres combine a group exercise, presentation, role-play and interview in one day. What each tests, what to say, and how to pace yourself.
- [What is a behavioral interview? How to prepare with STAR](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/behavioral-interview/index.md): Behavioral interviews ask 'tell me about a time'. Build a bank of 8–10 stories mapped to the competencies the job needs, and tell each one with STAR in 90 seconds.
- [How to prepare for a campus placement interview: complete guide](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/campus-placement-interview/index.md): Campus placements usually run aptitude, group discussion, technical and HR rounds. What each round checks, what freshers are asked, and a four-week prep plan.
- [What is a case interview? How to prepare and structure answers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/case-interview/index.md): A case interview gives you a business problem to solve out loud. How to clarify, structure, ask for data, do the maths aloud and deliver a recommendation.
- [What to say in an exit interview without burning bridges](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/exit-interview/index.md): Leaving a job? What to share and keep to yourself in an exit interview, how to turn criticism into useful feedback, and example answers to the usual questions.
- [Final round interview: what to expect and how to prepare](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/final-round-interview/index.md): The final round is usually with senior leaders: fewer skill questions, more judgement and fit, a closing case for you, and often the first real salary talk.
- [How to prepare for a group discussion (GD) round in an interview](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/group-discussion/index.md): The leaderless GD round in campus and MBA selection: when to open, how to add points and enter a crowded discussion, how to summarise, with example lines.
- [Group interview tips: how to stand out without talking over](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/group-interview/index.md): In a group interview, several candidates are assessed together. How to speak early, build on others, include quieter people and stand out without dominating.
- [What is an informational interview? Questions to ask](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/informational-interview/index.md): An informational interview is a short career chat where you ask the questions. How to request one, a 20-minute plan, the best questions to ask, and how to follow up.
- [How to prepare for an internal interview at your company](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/internal-interview/index.md): Interviewing for another role or team at your own employer: how to use inside knowledge, why not to assume they know your work, and how to answer 'why move?'
- [How to give a presentation in a job interview: tips and timing](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/interview-presentation/index.md): Asked to present in a job interview? A timed structure for a 10 or 15-minute slot, how many slides to use, how to rehearse to time, and how to handle the Q&A after.
- [One-way video interview tips: how to do a recorded interview](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/one-way-video-interview/index.md): In a one-way video interview you record answers to a timer with nobody on the other side. How to fit the clock, answer without follow-ups, and use retakes well.
- [How to prepare for a panel interview: tips for answering a group](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/panel-interview/index.md): Answer several interviewers at once: who to look at, how to handle handoffs between panelists, and how to read the hiring manager, HR, peer and senior roles.
- [How to prepare for a phone interview: tips and common questions](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/phone-interview/index.md): Prepare for a first-round phone screen: a quiet voice-only setup, a one-page note sheet, the questions screeners ask, and how to sound clear without a face.
- [Promotion interview: how to prepare and make your case to move up](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/promotion-interview/index.md): Interviewing for a higher level in your own team? Show you already work at the next level: evidence to gather, how to answer 'why you?', and leading former peers.
- [What to expect in a second interview and how to prepare for it](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/second-interview/index.md): A second interview goes deeper: harder follow-ups, meeting the team, sometimes a task. What changes from round one and how to prepare in the three days before.
- [What is a stress interview? How to stay calm and answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/stress-interview/index.md): A stress interview uses deliberate pressure: silence, interruptions, challenges, rudeness. Why some employers do it, the common tactics, and steady lines to reply.
- [How to prepare for a technical interview: thinking out loud](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/technical-interview/index.md): In a technical interview your reasoning is scored as much as your answer. How to narrate your thinking, ask clarifying questions, handle silence and admit gaps.
- [How to prepare for a US visa interview: questions and tips](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/us-visa-interview/index.md): General tips to speak clearly and briefly at a US visa interview: the kinds of questions asked, how to answer honestly in plain English, and where to find the rules.
- [Video interview tips: how to prepare for a Zoom or Teams call](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/interviews/video-interview/index.md): Prepare for a live video interview on Zoom, Teams or Meet: camera and light setup, where to look, handling lag and pauses, and what to say when the tech fails.

## Speeches and toasts

- [What to Say in a 50th Birthday Speech: Ideas and Examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/50th-birthday-speech/index.md): What to say at a 50th or other milestone birthday: fit five decades into three minutes, tease gently, honour the person. Structures and example speeches.
- [How to Give an Acceptance Speech for an Award or Honor](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/acceptance-speech/index.md): What to say when you accept an award: thank the organisers, a few people by name, say what it means and close, all in 1 to 2 minutes. Work and school examples.
- [What to Say in an Anniversary Speech for Parents or Spouse](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/anniversary-speech/index.md): What to say at a 25th, 40th or 50th wedding anniversary as a son, daughter or spouse: a simple structure, example speeches, and how to tell their story.
- [How to Present an Award: What to Say Before the Winner](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/award-presentation-speech/index.md): What to say when presenting an award: why the award matters, why this person earned it, and how to announce the name. Timings and example scripts.
- [What to Say in a Bar or Bat Mitzvah Speech (Parent or Teen)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/bar-mitzvah-speech/index.md): What parents say to their child at a bar or bat mitzvah, and how the teen shapes their own speech: the Torah portion, family, thanks, length and examples.
- [How to Write a Best Man Speech (With Examples and Timing)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/best-man-speech/index.md): A best man speech structure that fits 3 to 5 minutes: who you are, one or two stories about the groom, the turn to the couple, and the toast. Example lines.
- [What to Say in a Birthday Toast: Short Examples for Friends](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/birthday-toast/index.md): Short birthday toasts for a friend, partner, parent or sibling: a 30 to 90 second formula, funny and heartfelt examples, and how to raise the glass at dinner.
- [What Should the Bride Say in a Wedding Speech? Examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/bride-speech/index.md): What a bride says in her wedding speech: who to thank, what to say to your new spouse, lines for friends and family, example speeches and how long to talk.
- [What to Say in a Christmas or Holiday Party Speech at Work](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/christmas-party-speech/index.md): What a manager or host says at the work Christmas or holiday party: the year's wins, real thank-yous, an inclusive tone and a short finish. With examples.
- [How to Give Closing Remarks at an Event or Conference](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/closing-remarks/index.md): What to say in closing remarks: sum up key moments, thank speakers, sponsors and organisers, give next steps and end cleanly. Structure and example scripts.
- [What to Say in an Engagement Party Toast (With Examples)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/engagement-party-toast/index.md): What to say when you toast a newly engaged couple, as host parent or friend: a short structure, how-they-met lines, example toasts and what to save.
- [How to Write a Eulogy for a Friend: What to Say and Examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/eulogy-for-a-friend/index.md): How to write a eulogy for a close friend, including one who died young: what to include, how to use humour, speaking to their family, and examples.
- [How to Write a Eulogy for a Grandparent (Grandma or Grandpa)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/eulogy-for-a-grandparent/index.md): How to write a eulogy for your grandmother or grandfather: fitting a long life into 5 minutes, speaking as a grandchild, and an example eulogy.
- [How to Write a Eulogy for Your Mom or Dad (With Examples)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/eulogy-for-a-parent/index.md): How to write a eulogy for your mother or father: speak as their child, choose family memories, coordinate with siblings and stay composed. Example passages.
- [How to Write a Eulogy: Step-by-Step Guide With Examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/eulogy/index.md): How to write and deliver a eulogy for anyone: gathering stories, a simple structure, how long to speak, example lines and how to get through it on the day.
- [What to Say in a Farewell Speech When You Leave a Job](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/farewell-speech/index.md): What to say on your last day at a job: thank people, share one memory, say how to stay in touch, all in under three minutes. Examples for any reason.
- [How to Write a Father of the Bride Speech (With Examples)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/speeches/father-of-the-bride-speech/index.md): What a father of the bride should say: welcome guests as host, thank people, share one childhood memory, welcome the new spouse and give the toast. Examples.

Outline and examples.

## Presentations and pitches

- [How to Structure a 5-Minute Presentation (Word Count Too)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/5-minute-presentation/index.md): Fit any topic into 5 minutes: about 650–750 spoken words, 3–5 slides, a second-by-second structure, and a checklist of what to cut when you run over.
- [How to Present to Executives or a Board: Get to the Point](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/board-presentation/index.md): Present to senior leaders or a board: lead with the decision you need, tell a one-page story, expect interruptions, and give short answers to tough questions.
- [How to Give a Conference Talk: From Abstract to Q&A](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/conference-talk/index.md): Give a 20–40 minute conference talk: write an abstract that promises one takeaway, build a story arc, rehearse on a schedule, and handle audience questions.
- [How to Write an Elevator Pitch About Yourself (30 Seconds)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/elevator-pitch/index.md): Write a 30-second elevator pitch about yourself: who you are, what you do, what you want. Word counts, a fill-in template and examples for recruiters and new contacts.
- [How to Do a Group Presentation: Split Parts and Handoffs](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/group-presentation/index.md): Present as a group or team: split sections by strength, write smooth handoff lines between speakers, rehearse together, and agree who answers which questions.
- [How to Pitch to Investors: What to Say in Your Startup Pitch](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/investor-pitch/index.md): What to say when you pitch your startup to VCs or angels: problem, solution, traction and the ask, a spoken example, timing, and how to answer investor questions.
- [How to Prepare a Presentation for a Job Interview (Examples)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/job-interview-presentation/index.md): Prepare a job interview presentation: pick the right angle for the brief, build a 10–15 minute outline, and get ready for the panel's questions. With examples.
- [How to Give a Keynote Speech: Structure, Story and Delivery](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/keynote/index.md): Deliver a 30–60 minute keynote as the headline speaker: pick a big theme, build it from personal stories, plan changes of pace, and use the stage with confidence.
- [How to Give a Lightning Talk: 5 Minutes, One Point, No Filler](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/lightning-talk/index.md): Give a 5-minute lightning talk at a meetup or conference: pick one point, plan auto-advancing slides like Ignite's 20 x 15 seconds, and rehearse tightly to time.
- [How to Present a Research Poster: What to Say in 2 Minutes](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/poster-presentation/index.md): What to say when someone stops at your academic poster: a 30-second and 2-minute walkthrough, example scripts, how to start the conversation and common questions.
- [How to Give a Product Demo That Doesn't Bore Your Audience](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/product-demo/index.md): Run a live product or software demo customers stay awake for: follow one user's story, show outcomes before features, narrate clicks, and recover calmly when it breaks.
- [How to Run a Project Kickoff Meeting: What to Present and Say](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/project-kickoff/index.md): What to say when you kick off a project with a team or client: goals, scope, roles, timeline, risks and ways of working, with a 60-minute agenda and example lines.
- [How to Present a Quarterly Business Review (QBR) to Clients](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/quarterly-business-review/index.md): Run a QBR with a client or internally: results against goals, what changed, next quarter's plan, a timed agenda, and how to keep it a dialogue.
- [How to Give a Sales Pitch That Sounds Like a Conversation](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/sales-pitch/index.md): Pitch a product to a prospect in a meeting or call without sounding scripted: ask discovery questions first, describe value in their words, and handle objections calmly.
- [How to Give a Good Presentation at School Without Notes](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/school-presentation/index.md): Give a class presentation without reading your notes: learn it as a few key points, use slides as prompts, handle nerves, and know what teachers usually grade.
- [How to Give a Clear Update in a Team Meeting (With Examples)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/team-meeting-update/index.md): Give a short status update in standup or a weekly meeting: done, next, blocked, in under 60 seconds. Examples by role, rewrites and how to share bad news.
- [How to Give a TED-Style Talk: One Idea in 18 Minutes or Less](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/ted-style-talk/index.md): Give a TEDx or TED-style talk: find one idea worth sharing, build it step by step, decide whether to memorise, open strongly and stay under 18 minutes.
- [How to Prepare for a Thesis Defense: Presentation and Q&A](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/thesis-defense/index.md): Prepare for your master's thesis or PhD defense: a slide structure that fits 20–45 minutes, how to time it, and how to answer committee questions calmly.
- [How to Present a Training Session or Workshop to Adults](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/training-session/index.md): Deliver a training session or workshop to colleagues: a teach-show-practice structure, timings for 60 and 90 minutes, how to check understanding, and how to pace it.
- [How to Present a Webinar That Keeps People Watching](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/presentations/webinar/index.md): Host or present a webinar people don't leave: a minute-by-minute run of show, talking to a camera, keeping your energy up with no audience, and handling chat Q&A.

- [How to Talk to Your Crush Without Freezing Up (What to Say)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/small-talk/talking-to-your-crush/index.md): What to say to someone you like: how to start the first real conversation, lines that keep it light, how to show interest, and what to do when you freeze.

- [What to Talk About at Lunch With Coworkers or a New Team](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/small-talk/team-lunch/index.md): What to talk about at lunch with coworkers or a new team: group topics beyond work, questions that include everyone, what to avoid, and tips for new joiners.
- [Should You Talk to Your Uber Driver? What to Say in a Ride](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/small-talk/uber-driver/index.md): Whether to chat with your Uber, Lyft or taxi driver, how to tell if they want to talk, and what to say on a 5, 15 or 40-minute ride.
- [What to Say at the Start of a Zoom Call Before It Begins](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/small-talk/video-call-small-talk/index.md): What to say in the first minutes of a Zoom or Teams call while people join: openers for one-to-ones, team calls and client calls, and how to move to the agenda.
- [How to Make Small Talk at a Wedding Table Full of Strangers](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/small-talk/wedding-reception-small-talk/index.md): What to say when you're seated with strangers at a wedding: how to open, where to go after 'How do you know the couple?', and how to bring the whole table in.
- [How to Answer 'What Do You Do?' Without Being Boring](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/small-talk/what-do-you-do/index.md): How to answer 'So, what do you do?' at a party: a three-part reply, with examples for office jobs, students, parents, the unemployed and the self-employed.
- [What to Talk About at a Work Holiday Party (Without Talking Work)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/small-talk/work-holiday-party/index.md): What to say at the office holiday party to coworkers, their partners and senior people, with topics beyond work, example lines and the mistakes people regret.

## Speaking skills guides

- [How to Answer a Question When You Don't Know the Answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/answer-question-you-dont-know/index.md): What to say when you don't know the answer in an interview, meeting or Q&A: honest phrases, partial answers and follow-up promises that sound competent.
- [How to Calm Nerves Before a Job Interview: Night and Morning](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/calm-nerves-before-interview/index.md): A timeline for calming interview nerves, from the night before to the first minute in the room: prep, a warm-up answer, breathing and what to do if you blank.
- [CAR Method for Interviews: Shorter Answers Than STAR](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/car-method/index.md): When to use the CAR method (Challenge, Action, Result) instead of STAR, with the same story told both ways, timing, and how to turn CAR into resume bullets.
- [How to Write an Elevator Pitch About Yourself (With Examples)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/elevator-pitch/index.md): Write and say a 30 to 60 second pitch about yourself: a fill-in template, examples for a student, career changer and founder, and how to sound unrehearsed.
- [How to Make Eye Contact on Video Calls and Zoom Interviews](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/eye-contact-on-video-calls/index.md): How to look like you're making eye contact on camera: camera height and distance, where to put notes, when to look at faces, and a two-minute setup check.
- [How to Breathe While Speaking So You Don't Run Out of Air](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-breathe-while-speaking/index.md): Why you run out of breath mid-sentence and how to fix it: breathing at phrase breaks, belly breathing, shorter sentences, and read-aloud drills to practice.
- [How to End a Presentation Strongly (Not With Any Questions)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-end-a-presentation/index.md): How to close a talk so it sticks: the summary-plus-ask ending, where Q&A goes, example last lines, and why 'that's it' and 'any questions?' fall flat.
- [How to Explain Complex Ideas Simply to Any Audience](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-explain-things-simply/index.md): How to explain something technical to non-experts: a one-sentence summary first, analogies, a jargon swap list, checking understanding, and an example.
- [How to Give a Toast at a Wedding or Dinner (Short Examples)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-give-a-toast/index.md): What to say in a toast and how long it should be: a 1-2 minute structure, example toasts for a wedding, birthday and leaving do, and how to raise the glass.
- [How to Give an Impromptu Speech With No Preparation](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-give-an-impromptu-speech/index.md): What to say when asked to 'say a few words' with no warning: three quick frameworks, a one-minute shape, opening lines that buy time and practice prompts.
- [How to Handle Q&A After a Presentation, Tough Questions Too](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-handle-q-and-a/index.md): How to handle Q&A after a talk: predict likely questions, use repeat-answer-bridge, stay calm with hostile or unanswerable ones, and end on your point.
- [How to Improve Public Speaking Skills: A 30-Day Practice Plan](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-improve-public-speaking-skills/index.md): A day-by-day 30-day plan of short out-loud drills covering pace, fillers, structure, voice, nerves and delivery, with a recorded test on day 1 and day 30.
- [How to Introduce Yourself in a Meeting or at an Event](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-introduce-yourself/index.md): What to say in a 10-second self-introduction at a meeting, class or networking event: the name, role, hook formula, with example lines for each setting.
- [How to Keep a Conversation Going When It Starts to Die](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-keep-a-conversation-going/index.md): What to say when a conversation goes quiet: six follow-up question patterns, threading off details, how much to share about yourself, and graceful exits.
- [How to Make Small Talk With Anyone Without It Feeling Awkward](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-make-small-talk/index.md): How to start small talk with a stranger or coworker: opening lines for the office, events and parties, what to say after the first reply, and topics to skip.
- [How to Practice a Speech: A Rehearsal Plan That Works](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-practice-a-speech/index.md): A day-by-day rehearsal plan for any speech: how many run-throughs, out loud vs in your head, timing runs, drilling the hard parts and a real dress rehearsal.
- [How to Present Online and Keep People Engaged on Zoom](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-present-online/index.md): How to give a virtual presentation people pay attention to: energy for the camera, interaction every few minutes, cleaner slide sharing, and handling the chat.
- [How to Project Your Voice Without Shouting or Straining](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-project-your-voice/index.md): Get louder and carry across a room without straining: breath support, resonance and aiming exercises, plus quick checks for a big room versus a meeting table.
- [How to Slow Down When You Talk Too Fast, Especially When Nervous](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-slow-down-when-speaking/index.md): Stop talking too fast: measure your words per minute, learn the target range for talks and conversation, and use marked pauses and sentence breaks to slow down.
- [How to Speak More Clearly and Stop Mumbling When You Talk](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-speak-clearly/index.md): Stop mumbling and be easier to understand: drills for mouth opening, word endings, volume and pace, plus tongue twisters and a daily read-aloud exercise.
- [How to Speak Up in Meetings When You're Quiet or New](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-speak-up-in-meetings/index.md): How to contribute in meetings when you hesitate: when to jump in, short sentence starters, how to interrupt politely and how to prepare one point beforehand.
- [How to Speak With Confidence in Everyday Conversations](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-speak-with-confidence/index.md): Sound confident at work and with friends, not just on stage: posture, volume, finishing your sentences and dropping hedges, with before and after lines to copy.
- [How to Start a Speech: Opening Lines That Grab Attention](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-start-a-speech/index.md): What the first 30 seconds of a speech should do, seven ways to open (question, story, number, bold claim and more) with example lines, and openings to avoid.
- [How to Stop Rambling When You Talk and Get to the Point](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-stop-rambling/index.md): Why you ramble and how to stop: answer point first, test your headline in one breath, land your last sentence and stop. With a rambling vs tight example.
- [How to Stop Saying 'Like' and 'You Know' All the Time](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-stop-saying-like/index.md): How to cut 'like', 'you know', 'basically' and 'so' from your speech: why they differ from um, what each one does, what to say instead, and a tracking drill.
- [How to Stop Sounding Monotone: Add Variety to Your Voice](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-stop-sounding-monotone/index.md): How to make a flat, monotone voice more interesting: pitch, pace and volume drills, how to mark a script for emphasis, and how to hear yourself honestly.
- [How to Stop Your Voice Shaking When You're Nervous](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-stop-voice-shaking/index.md): Why your voice shakes when you're nervous and how to steady it: breath, a slower start, an easy volume, warm-ups, and a 2-minute routine before you speak.
- [How to Structure a Presentation: Simple Outlines That Work](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-structure-a-presentation/index.md): Four presentation outlines (problem-solution, past-present-future, three points and story) with minute-by-minute timing for 5, 10 and 20 minute talks.
- [How to Think on Your Feet When You're Put on the Spot](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-think-on-your-feet/index.md): Answer well when asked something unexpected in a meeting or interview: honest buy-time phrases, a structure you can pick in 3 seconds, and drills for speed.
- [How to Use Pauses in a Speech for Emphasis and Control](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/how-to-use-pauses/index.md): Where to pause in a speech and for how long: pause types with seconds, how to mark them in a script, drills to get used to silence, and common mistakes.
- [Should You Memorize a Speech or Use Notes? How to Decide](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/memorize-speech-or-use-notes/index.md): Memorize word for word, use notes or speak from an outline? A comparison by situation (toast, pitch, keynote, class) and how to make notes you can glance at.
- [What to Do When Your Mind Goes Blank While Speaking](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/mind-goes-blank-while-speaking/index.md): What to do the moment you freeze mid-sentence: recovery lines to say out loud, how to find your place again, and anchors that make blanking less likely.
- [PREP Method: How to Give a Clear Answer in 30 Seconds](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/prep-method/index.md): How to use PREP (Point, Reason, Example, Point) for opinion questions, meetings and on-the-spot answers: a fill-in template, timing and worked examples.
- [How to Overcome Fear of Public Speaking and Stage Fright](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/public-speaking-anxiety/index.md): Get over fear of speaking in front of people with a gradual exposure ladder, from one listener to a full room, plus what to do in the last 10 minutes.
- [How to Record Yourself Speaking and Review It Honestly](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/record-yourself-speaking/index.md): How to use recordings of yourself to improve: a simple setup, a checklist for each playback (pace, fillers, pauses, openings), and getting past the cringe.
- [How to Be Understood Clearly When You Speak With an Accent](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/speaking-clearly-with-an-accent/index.md): How to make sure people understand you with your accent, without changing who you are: pace, word stress, word endings, names and numbers, checking in.
- [STAR Method: How to Answer Behavioral Interview Questions](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/star-method/index.md): Build a STAR interview answer step by step: seconds for each part, a worked example from rough story to final answer, and the mistakes that make it run long.
- [How to Stop Saying Um and Uh When You Speak (Practical Steps)](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/stop-saying-um/index.md): Why you say um and uh, the pause-instead drill that replaces them, and a four-week count-and-cut plan using a free filler word counter. Aim for fewer, not zero.
- [How to Tell a Story in a Presentation People Remember](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/storytelling-in-presentations/index.md): How to use a short story in a work talk or pitch: a 60-second story arc, where to place it, details that make it land and how to cut a story that drags.
- [What to Do With Your Hands When Giving a Presentation](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/guides/what-to-do-with-your-hands/index.md): Where to put your hands while presenting: a neutral rest position, gestures that match your words, habits to drop like pockets and clasping, and tips for video.

## Speaking and interview glossary

- [What is active listening? Definition and example responses](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/active-listening/index.md): What active listening means in conversation, its five parts, and example responses that show you heard someone, plus what it is not.
- [What is an anecdote in a speech? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/anecdote/index.md): What an anecdote is in a speech, how it differs from a full story or a general example, a short sample anecdote, and how to tell one in under a minute.
- [What is articulation in speaking? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/articulation/index.md): Articulation is how clearly you shape sounds and word endings. See clear vs slurred speech examples, why it matters on calls, and a 2-minute warm-up.
- [What is a behavioral interview? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/behavioral-interview/index.md): A behavioral interview defined: what it asks, how it differs from situational, technical and case interviews, and sample questions you'll likely hear.
- [What does BLUF mean? Bottom line up front, definition and example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/bluf/index.md): BLUF means bottom line up front: lead with your main point or request, then the details. See where it comes from and an example spoken update, before and after.
- [What is body language? Definition and examples in speaking](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/body-language/index.md): Body language defined, with speaking examples: stance, gestures, face and eye contact, what each often signals to listeners, and on video calls.
- [What is cadence in speaking? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/cadence/index.md): Cadence is the rhythm and flow of speech: how pace, pauses and stress rise and fall. See choppy, sing-song and smooth cadence examples and how to fix yours.
- [What is a call to action in a speech? Definition and example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/call-to-action/index.md): What a call to action is at the end of a speech or presentation, what makes one work, and example closing lines for work talks, class and events.
- [What is the CAR method? Definition and example answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/car-method/index.md): The CAR method answers interview questions in three parts: Challenge, Action, Result. See what each part means and one compact example answer under a minute.
- [What is a case interview? Definition and example question](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/case-interview/index.md): What a case interview is, a made-up example case prompt, and how to talk through it out loud step by step, with example lines for each stage.
- [What is a closed question? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/closed-question/index.md): What a closed question is, examples of yes/no, either/or and short-fact questions, and when closed questions are more useful than open ones.
- [What is a competency-based interview? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/competency-based-interview/index.md): A competency-based interview tests set skills like teamwork or decision-making with past examples. See common competencies, example questions and scoring.
- [What is diaphragmatic breathing for speaking? Definition](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/diaphragmatic-breathing/index.md): Diaphragmatic (belly) breathing supports your voice when you speak. See what it is, how it differs from chest breathing, and a simple 3-minute practice exercise.
- [What is diction in speaking? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/diction/index.md): Diction means two things: the words you choose and how clearly you pronounce them. See examples of each, with plain and formal word choices and clear speech.
- [What is an elevator pitch? Definition and example script](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/elevator-pitch/index.md): What an elevator pitch is, how long it should be in seconds and words, what goes in it, and one example script you can adapt out loud.
- [What are ethos, pathos and logos? Definitions and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/ethos-pathos-logos/index.md): Ethos, pathos and logos defined: the three rhetorical appeals, each with an example line from one made-up talk, and how speakers balance them.
- [What is executive presence? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/executive-presence/index.md): What people mean by executive presence, the speaking behaviours usually linked to it with example lines, and the fair criticisms of the term.
- [What is an extemporaneous speech? Definition and example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/extemporaneous-speech/index.md): An extemporaneous speech is prepared and rehearsed but not memorised: you speak from brief notes. See how it differs from impromptu speaking and an example note card.
- [What are filler words? Definition and list of examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/filler-words/index.md): Filler words defined, with a list of common ones (um, uh, like, you know, so, basically), why speakers use them, and how to count your own.
- [What is a follow-up question? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/follow-up-question/index.md): A follow-up question builds on what someone just said. See types of follow-ups with examples for small talk, and the follow-ups interviewers ask and you can ask.
- [What is glossophobia? Definition of fear of public speaking](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/glossophobia/index.md): Glossophobia is the term for fear of public speaking. What the word means, common signs before and during a talk, and where to read more. Not medical advice.
- [What is hedging language? Definition and examples of hedge words](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/hedging-language/index.md): Hedging language softens what you say: just, maybe, I think, sort of. See common hedge words, before-and-after examples, and when hedging helps or weakens you.
- [What is an icebreaker? Definition and examples for meetings](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/icebreaker/index.md): What an icebreaker is, example questions for team meetings, workshops, events and video calls, and what makes an icebreaker work or fall flat.
- [What is impostor syndrome? Definition and example when speaking](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/impostor-syndrome/index.md): Impostor syndrome explained in plain terms: what it is, how it sounds when you present or interview, and steadier phrasing. General info, not medical advice.
- [What is an impromptu speech? Definition and example topics](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/impromptu-speech/index.md): An impromptu speech is a short talk given with little or no preparation. See a definition, how it differs from prepared speeches, and 15 example topics to practise.
- [What is an informational interview? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/informational-interview/index.md): What an informational interview is, who asks for one and why, how it differs from a job interview, and example questions to ask in 20 minutes.
- [What is an informative speech? Definition and example topics](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/informative-speech/index.md): What an informative speech is, its main types, how it differs from a persuasive speech on the same topic, and example topics for class and work.
- [What is intonation in speaking? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/intonation/index.md): Intonation explained: how pitch rises and falls across a sentence, what it signals, and examples of statements versus questions and lists in English.
- [What is a keynote speech? Definition and example structure](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/keynote-speech/index.md): A keynote speech is the main talk that sets the theme of an event. See typical lengths, a minute-by-minute example structure and how it differs from other talks.
- [What is mirroring in conversation? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/mirroring/index.md): Mirroring means subtly matching someone's posture, energy or words to build connection. See examples of body, voice and verbal mirroring, and when it backfires.
- [What is a mock interview? Definition and how it works](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/mock-interview/index.md): What a mock interview is, how one runs step by step, who can run it (a friend, a career office, a coach or an AI partner) and what you get from it.
- [What does monotone mean in speaking? Definition and example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/monotone/index.md): What a monotone voice is, why it happens (scripts, nerves, tiredness), and how a sample line sounds flat versus varied. Fixes are in the linked guide.
- [What is Monroe's motivated sequence? Definition and example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/monroes-motivated-sequence/index.md): Monroe's motivated sequence is a five-step persuasive structure: attention, need, satisfaction, visualization, action. See each step with a short example line.
- [What is an open-ended question? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/open-ended-question/index.md): What an open-ended question is, how it differs from a closed question, and examples you can use in conversation, small talk and job interviews.
- [What is a panel interview? Definition and what to expect](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/panel-interview/index.md): A panel interview defined: who usually sits on the panel, what each person listens for, and how answering a group differs from a one-to-one interview.
- [What is paraphrasing in conversation? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/paraphrasing/index.md): Paraphrasing as a listening skill: what it means to reflect back what someone said, example lines for work, friends and customers, and when to use it.
- [What is a pause in public speaking? Definition and example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/pause/index.md): A deliberate pause is a silence you use on purpose to land a point, separate ideas or replace a filler word. See pause types, typical lengths and a marked example.
- [What is Pecha Kucha? Definition and example presentation format](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/pecha-kucha/index.md): Pecha Kucha is 20 slides shown for 20 seconds each, a 6 minute 40 second talk. See the rules, words per slide, where it came from and an example topic plan.
- [What is a persuasive speech? Definition and example outline](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/persuasive-speech/index.md): What a persuasive speech is, how it differs from an informative speech, the three common types, and a short example outline with timings for 5 minutes.
- [What is a phone screen interview? Definition and what to expect](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/phone-screen/index.md): What a recruiter phone screen is, how long it usually lasts, the questions to expect and why, and how speaking on the phone differs from in person.
- [What is a pitch deck? Definition and example slide outline](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/pitch-deck/index.md): What a pitch deck is, the usual slide order with what to say on each slide, and how founders present a deck out loud to investors.
- [What is the PREP method? Definition and example answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/prep-method/index.md): The PREP method gives a clear answer in four parts: Point, Reason, Example, Point. See what each part does and one compact example answer under a minute.
- [What is the pyramid principle? Definition and spoken example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/pyramid-principle/index.md): The pyramid principle structures communication answer-first: main point, then grouped reasons, then details. See the shape and an example spoken update.
- [What does building rapport mean? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/rapport/index.md): What rapport means in conversation and job interviews, specific behaviours that build it with example lines, and the common habits that break it.
- [What is a rhetorical question? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/rhetorical-question/index.md): What a rhetorical question is, example rhetorical questions from speeches and presentations, and when they work as an opener or fall flat.
- [What is the rule of three in speaking? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/rule-of-three/index.md): The rule of three means grouping ideas, examples or words in threes so they're easy to follow and remember. See example lines for toasts, updates and pitches.
- [What is signposting in a presentation? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/signposting/index.md): Signposting means using short phrases that tell listeners where you are in a talk. See a list of example signposts for previewing, moving on, contrasting and closing.
- [What is a situational interview? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/situational-interview/index.md): A situational interview asks 'what would you do if…' questions about likely job scenarios. See examples by role and how they differ from behavioral questions.
- [What is small talk? Definition and examples of good topics](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/small-talk/index.md): Small talk defined: what light conversation is for, good topics with example lines you can say, and the topics most people avoid with strangers.
- [What are speaker notes? Definition and example for presentations](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/speaker-notes/index.md): Speaker notes are the private notes under each slide that only you see while presenting. See what good bullet-style notes look like versus a full script.
- [What is a hook in a speech? Definition and opening examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/speech-hook/index.md): A speech hook is the opening line that makes the audience want to keep listening. See six types of hook, a short example of each, and openings to avoid.
- [What is stage fright? Definition, signs and example](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/stage-fright/index.md): Stage fright is the fear and physical stress of performing in front of others: speaking, music, acting or sport. Learn the signs and how it differs from glossophobia.
- [What is the STAR method? Definition and example answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/star-method/index.md): The STAR method defined: Situation, Task, Action, Result. What each part means, how much time each deserves, and one compact example answer.
- [What is the STARR method? Definition and example answer](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/starr-method/index.md): The STARR method is STAR plus Reflection: Situation, Task, Action, Result, Reflection. See what the extra R adds and example closing lines that work.
- [What is a stress interview? Definition and example questions](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/stress-interview/index.md): A stress interview deliberately puts pressure on candidates to see how they react. See common tactics, example questions and calm ways to respond.
- [What is uptalk? Definition and example of rising intonation](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/uptalk/index.md): Uptalk means ending a statement with a rising pitch, as if asking a question. See an example, how listeners may hear it, and how to check your own.
- [What is vocal fry? Definition and example in speaking](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/vocal-fry/index.md): What vocal fry sounds like, why it happens at the ends of sentences, and how listeners may hear it on calls and recordings. No judgment of anyone's voice.
- [What is vocal projection? Definition and example in speaking](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/vocal-projection/index.md): Vocal projection means making your voice carry to the back of a room with breath support, not by shouting. See projection vs shouting and an example room check.
- [What is vocal variety? Definition and examples in speeches](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/vocal-variety/index.md): Vocal variety means changing your pitch, pace, volume and pauses as you speak. See one example line said five ways and how each change shifts the meaning.
- [What is words per minute in speaking? Definition and examples](https://www.orecci.com/speaking-coach/glossary/words-per-minute/index.md): Words per minute (wpm) measures speaking pace. See typical ranges for conversation and presentations, how to calculate yours, and worked examples.
